title: 5. Types of Deserts Based on Surface

blocks.content: Hamada or Rocky Deserts consist of bare, exposed bedrock stripped of fine material by persistent wind deflation.

rows: Vast undulating sand dunes; known as Koum in Turkestan
Gravel plains; known as Serir (Libya) and Gibber (Australia)
Smooth, windswept rock pavements stripped of fine particles

items: Competitive exams often test local terminology: Erg (Sahara/Turkestan), Serir (Libya), and Gibber (Australia).
Distinguish clearly between wind deflation (removal of fine dust) and abrasion (sandblasting action on rock surfaces).
Hamada deserts feature exposed bedrock pavements, whereas Erg deserts are characterized by mobile sand dunes.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Erg or Sandy Deserts are vast seas of sand dominated by wind-deposited dunes.
Reg or Stony Deserts feature surfaces covered with angular gravel and pebbles, locally called Serir in Libya and Gibber in Australia.
Hamada or Rocky Deserts consist of bare, exposed bedrock stripped of fine material by persistent wind deflation.
Deflation and abrasion are the primary aeolian processes shaping these desert surface types.
